title: Explaining a place to a visitor
instructions: Complete the vocabulary and question practice in the anchors first, for up to four minutes. Record the three opening answers for about 20 seconds each. Then take exactly one minute for keyword notes on the card and speak for one to two minutes, stopping at two minutes. Answer the final follow-up briefly. This combines a Part 1 language bridge with Part 2 practice; it is not a full speaking test. After feedback, one supported retry of the long turn is allowed.

stimulus.text:
First, answer three short familiar-topic questions about your home area. Then complete the longer task.
Part 2 task card
Describe a place in or near your home area that you would show a visitor.
You should say:
- what kind of place it is
- how someone can reach it
- what the visitor could do there
and explain why you would choose that place.
Follow-up: Would you choose a different place in bad weather?

questions.prompt: What kinds of places do people visit in your home area?
Why do you enjoy or dislike one of those places?
Would you suggest an indoor or an outdoor activity to a visitor?
Give the long turn using the task card.
Would you choose a different place in bad weather?

teachingAnchors.label: Build a topic map with meaning
teachingAnchors.text: Sort your own local-place words under travel, activities and facilities. Choose one thing you value, one difficulty and one feature you would like to have. Explain each with a short phrase. Then make a what, a why and a would question from different branches and answer each aloud; a would question needs a possible choice, not merely a current fact.

teachingAnchors.label: Connect description and explanation
teachingAnchors.text: Take a new keyword such as “shelter”. Say what it offers, who might need it and why. Add only details that help that listener. Turn the three fragments into brief connected speech, then remove written sentences and retain keywords for the card. This adapts familiar-question practice into a longer task rather than asking you to memorise a sample answer.

teachingAnchors.label: Practise stress in your own message
teachingAnchors.text: With a teacher or approved audio model, compare the stressed syllable in “location” and “visitor”. Put each in a new sentence about a place, record and check whether a listener identifies the word easily. Keep that word in a meaningful sentence when you retry. Written capital letters alone do not establish pronunciation.

criteria.label: Fluency and coherence
criteria.description: Use the actual recording to review continuity, appropriate pauses, repair and logical connections. Describe where the listener could or could not follow the answer. A transcript cannot establish speed, pause length or spoken fluency. Do not reward length or rehearsed linking phrases alone.

criteria.label: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Check whether vocabulary expresses the intended meaning accurately and appropriately, and whether the speaker can paraphrase a missing word. Identify a specific successful choice and one usable alternative; rare vocabulary is not a goal by itself.

criteria.label: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Review the structures actually used and whether errors obscure time, relationships or meaning. Quote a short learner-produced example in private feedback and offer one targeted repair. Do not infer range from prompt difficulty.

criteria.label: Pronunciation
criteria.description: Assess only from usable actual audio: intelligibility, word stress, rhythm, connected speech and sounds in context. Note the segment requiring listener effort and a focused practice action. Accent identity is not an error; if audio is missing or unclear, withhold this judgement.

assessment.feedbackGuidance: Check whether the three opening answers respond to what, why and would rather than using the same generic speech. In the long turn, locate a precise place description, a clear route and a reason linked to the visitor’s needs. Do not require equal time for every cue point. Choose one unclear word stress and one underdeveloped reason for the supported retry; use actual audio for the stress observation. All four qualitative criteria require teacher review; pronunciation and temporal fluency require usable audio. Do not infer a band from this drill or reward a memorised script. If only a transcript is available, withhold audio-dependent judgements.

locale.instructionsFa: ابتدا تمرین واژگان و پرسشِ راهنماها را حداکثر چهار دقیقه انجام دهید. سه پاسخ آغازین را هرکدام حدود ۲۰ ثانیه ضبط کنید. سپس دقیقاً یک دقیقه برای یادداشت کلیدی کارت فرصت دارید؛ یک تا دو دقیقه صحبت کنید و در دو دقیقه متوقف شوید. پیگیری آخر را کوتاه پاسخ دهید. این ترکیبِ تمرین زبان بخش اول و تمرین بخش دوم است، نه آزمون کامل. پس از بازخورد، یک تکرار حمایتی گفتار بلند مجاز است.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: نقشه معنایی موضوع بسازید
teachingAnchorsFa.text: واژه‌های مکان‌های اطراف را زیر رفت‌وآمد، فعالیت‌ها و امکانات دسته‌بندی کنید. یک نکته مطلوب، یک دشواری و یک امکان دلخواه انتخاب کنید و هرکدام را کوتاه توضیح دهید. از شاخه‌های متفاوت پرسش با what، why و would بسازید و بلند پاسخ دهید؛ would انتخاب ممکن می‌خواهد، نه فقط واقعیت فعلی.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: توصیف را به توضیح وصل کنید
teachingAnchorsFa.text: واژه کلیدی تازه‌ای مثل shelter انتخاب کنید. بگویید چه فراهم می‌کند، چه کسی نیاز دارد و چرا. فقط جزئیاتی اضافه کنید که به آن شنونده کمک می‌کند. سه قطعه را به گفتار کوتاه پیوسته تبدیل کنید؛ سپس جمله‌های نوشته‌شده را کنار بگذارید و فقط کلیدواژه نگه دارید. هدف تبدیل تمرین پرسش آشنا به گفتار بلندتر است، نه حفظ پاسخ نمونه.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: تکیه را در پیام خودتان تمرین کنید
teachingAnchorsFa.text: با مدرس یا مدل صوتی تأییدشده، هجای تکیه‌دار location و visitor را مقایسه کنید. هرکدام را در جمله تازه‌ای درباره مکان بگذارید، ضبط کنید و تشخیص آسان واژه توسط شنونده را بررسی کنید. در تکرار، واژه را در جمله معنادار نگه دارید. حروف بزرگ روی کاغذ به‌تنهایی تلفظ را ثابت نمی‌کند.

locale.feedbackGuidanceFa: بررسی کنید سه پاسخ آغازین واقعاً به چه، چرا و would پاسخ می‌دهند، نه اینکه یک گفتار کلی را تکرار کنند. در گفتار بلند، توصیف دقیق مکان، مسیر روشن و دلیل مرتبط با نیاز بازدیدکننده را پیدا کنید. برای هر نکته زمان برابر مطالبه نکنید. یک تکیه نامشخص و یک دلیل کم‌بسط را برای تلاش حمایتی انتخاب کنید؛ تکیه را از روی صدا بررسی کنید. چهار معیار کیفی به بازبینی مدرس نیاز دارند؛ تلفظ و روانی زمانی به صدای قابل استفاده نیاز دارند. از این تمرین بند استنباط نکنید و به متن حفظ‌شده پاداش ندهید. اگر فقط متن دارید، درباره ویژگی‌های وابسته به صدا داوری نکنید.

provenance.rightsNote: Source-based Mitooni adaptation for the authorized Iranian audience. Arash authorized full-corpus AI ingestion and synthesis. This unit documents the supplied-source pages actually used; no worldwide distribution authority is inferred.
provenance.transformationNotes: Selected Mindset pages were actually read before this revision. Teaching progression and semantic domain are adapted from those pages; all dialogue, lecture wording, named examples, questions and keys were newly authored. No source model answer or recording is republished. Foundation/Level1 jointly support the foundation pathway; other level mappings are authoring choices, not band equivalences.

objectiveMappings.sourceLearningPoint: Respond distinctly to WH/why/yes-no/would prompts about hometown and accommodation.
objectiveMappings.unitTeachingConnection: Both units include three short opening questions before the card; train explicitly categorises and generates questions, while transfer independently applies question focus.
objectiveMappings.taskTransformation: Source hometown/accommodation meaning categories become a visitor-place and away-from-home accommodation sequence, with new questions and no model transcript.

objectiveMappings.sourceLearningPoint: Organise place vocabulary by meaning and generate ideas from a topic map instead of relying on rehearsed answers.
objectiveMappings.unitTeachingConnection: Train builds map branches and connects feature/person/reason; the card extends that familiar-question practice to a long turn; transfer uses a different accommodation choice.
objectiveMappings.taskTransformation: The long-turn bridge is an explicit Mitooni extension of source Part1 idea-generation, not a claim that these selected pages themselves teach the entire Part2 construct.

objectiveMappings.sourceLearningPoint: Attend to syllable stress in topic vocabulary and practise it in speech.
objectiveMappings.unitTeachingConnection: Train checks new place-related words with an actual model/listener; post-submit transfer review identifies an audible stress target.
objectiveMappings.taskTransformation: Different lexical examples replace the source word list; pronunciation remains audio-dependent and no source audio is reused.

notes: Teacher/examiner review required: check prompt accessibility, natural follow-ups, sequencing and suitability for assigned pathway. Pathways are support levels, not calibrated IELTS bands.

Recording must be permitted and usable before spoken assessment; do not send learner audio to an external provider without the agreed consent/data boundary. Local authoring includes no recording or external audio call.

Before timing, provide an unscored microphone check and a clear retry path. Technical failure invalidates timing; retain work privately, mark the attempt interrupted and use a new prompt family for independent evidence. A repeated prompt after coaching is supported practice.

Agree access needs before starting. Permit a neutral topic alternative where personal disclosure would be uncomfortable; mark changed timing or transcript-only work explicitly rather than claiming equivalent independent speech evidence.
Qualitative practice feedback is not a calibrated examiner band. Pronunciation and temporal fluency cannot be assessed from a transcript.

Revision 2 supersedes the held original-only draft. Review source-objective-task fit against the selected Mindset pages; semantic domains and meaningful language practice are adapted, not merely format-cited.
No source model answer or recording is republished. Inspect English/Persian equivalence and use only actual consented recordings for spoken judgement.

Selected Level2 source pages teach familiar-topic Part1 language. This unit transparently extends that language into Part2 after a three-question bridge; teacher must review whether support is sufficient. It is not a claim of full source or Part2 coverage.
